questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A CI/CD pipeline needs to deploy CloudFormation stacks into a workload account. The current design stores a long-term IAM user's access key in the build project. What should replace this design?

answers.text: An IAM role assumed by the pipeline with scoped deployment permissions
A shared root user access key stored as a pipeline secret
A human IAM user reused by every pipeline
A resource tag that contains the access key

explanations.a: A role provides temporary credentials and can be scoped to the deployment actions and target resources instead of storing long-term keys. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Root access keys are excessive and create severe blast radius for automated deployment.
explanations.c: Shared human users weaken accountability and keep long-term credentials in automation.
explanations.d: Tags are visible metadata and are not a secure or functional credential mechanism.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A developer needs console access to troubleshoot staging but should not have permanent production permissions. Which IAM entity model is appropriate?

answers.text: Permanent access keys assigned directly to the developer for production
Federated human access to roles with time-bound or approval-based production elevation
An EC2 instance profile attached to the developer's laptop
A bucket policy granting the developer all AWS actions

explanations.a: Permanent keys increase exposure and do not provide controlled console elevation.
explanations.b: Human access should use federation and roles so permissions are temporary, auditable, and aligned to environment need. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Instance profiles are for AWS compute, not human workstation console access.
explanations.d: Bucket policies affect S3 resources and cannot grant all console permissions across AWS.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An application on EC2 must call DynamoDB. Which identity mechanism should be used?

answers.text: A plaintext IAM access key stored in the AMI
A developer's personal access key copied into user data
An IAM role attached through an EC2 instance profile
The account root credentials stored in an environment variable

explanations.a: AMI-baked keys spread long-term credentials to every instance created from the image.
explanations.b: Personal keys in user data create accountability and exposure problems.
explanations.c: An instance profile delivers temporary credentials to the instance without embedding static keys in the application. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Root credentials are too privileged and should not be used by workloads.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A Lambda function must read from an S3 bucket and write to a DynamoDB table. Which identity should grant this access?

answers.text: An IAM group assigned to the Lambda function
A console password embedded in the function package
An unrestricted administrator user created for the function
The Lambda execution role with only the required S3 and DynamoDB actions

explanations.a: IAM groups are for users and are not attached to Lambda functions.
explanations.b: Console passwords are human credentials and should not be packaged with code.
explanations.c: A long-term administrator user is unnecessary and unsafe for a Lambda workload.
explanations.d: The execution role is the machine identity for Lambda and should grant only the calls the function needs. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A third-party SaaS platform needs to read selected metrics from one AWS account. What is the preferred access model?

answers.text: Cross-account IAM role with an external ID and least-privilege permissions
An administrator access key emailed to the SaaS provider
A public CloudWatch dashboard that includes all account data
A shared root password stored in the SaaS configuration

explanations.a: A cross-account role with external ID reduces confused-deputy risk and avoids sharing long-term credentials. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Emailing administrator keys exposes long-term credentials and excessive permissions.
explanations.c: A public dashboard can expose broader operational information and does not provide API access control.
explanations.d: Root credentials should never be shared with an external provider.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A DevOps engineer is reviewing access for humans, applications, and AWS services. Which principle correctly separates IAM entity usage?

answers.text: Use IAM users with long-term keys for every workload and every employee
Use federated roles for humans, service roles for AWS services, and instance or task roles for workloads
Use security groups as the primary human identity store
Use S3 bucket ACLs to represent every machine identity

explanations.a: Long-term users increase rotation burden and are weaker for workloads and federated human access.
explanations.b: Different principals need identity mechanisms designed for their lifecycle, credential delivery, and audit requirements. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Security groups control network traffic and do not authenticate humans.
explanations.d: Bucket ACLs authorize S3 objects and do not provide machine identity across services.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A company uses an external identity provider and wants employees to access AWS accounts without creating IAM users in each account. Which solution fits?

answers.text: Separate IAM users created manually in every account
Shared administrator credentials for each team
AWS IAM Identity Center integrated with the identity provider
S3 bucket policies as the workforce login system

explanations.a: Per-account users create deprovisioning and access review challenges.
explanations.b: Shared credentials remove individual accountability and increase compromise risk.
explanations.c: IAM Identity Center enables federated workforce access to multiple AWS accounts through centralized permission assignments. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Bucket policies authorize S3 resources and do not provide workforce federation to AWS accounts.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A SAML provider is used for workforce federation. What should AWS receive after successful authentication?

answers.text: The user's corporate password stored inside IAM
A public SSH key that grants all AWS permissions
A CloudWatch log stream name used as the identity token
A federated assertion that maps the user to an allowed IAM role or permission set

explanations.a: Federation avoids storing corporate passwords directly in IAM.
explanations.b: SSH keys authenticate operating system access and do not authorize AWS API roles.
explanations.c: Log stream names are not federation assertions.
explanations.d: Federation relies on trusted assertions that let AWS issue temporary role-based access rather than permanent user credentials. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A DevOps team needs developers to switch between development and production roles using the same corporate identity. What should be configured?

answers.text: Permission sets or federated role mappings for each environment
One permanent production access key reused in both environments
Different shared passwords posted in team chat
A Lambda environment variable containing every developer name

explanations.a: Environment-specific assignments let the same workforce identity receive different temporary permissions by context. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: A reused key removes environment separation and increases blast radius.
explanations.c: Shared passwords are not auditable per person and expose credentials.
explanations.d: Environment variables do not provide federated role mapping.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A contractor should lose AWS access automatically when removed from the corporate directory group. Which design supports this?

answers.text: A standalone IAM user that nobody reviews
Federated access controlled by identity provider group membership
A permanent access key stored in the contractor's local tool
A security group rule named after the contractor

explanations.a: Standalone users can remain active after directory access is removed.
explanations.b: Group-driven federation ties AWS access to the central identity lifecycle, reducing stale account access. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Local long-term keys can persist after the contract ends.
explanations.d: Security group names do not control workforce authentication.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A multi-account organization wants central auditability of who accessed which account and role. What federation practice helps?

answers.text: Use one shared IAM user named developers
Disable CloudTrail for federation events
Use IAM Identity Center or federated roles with identifiable sessions and CloudTrail logging
Let users assume roles from anonymous web identities

explanations.a: Shared users make it difficult to attribute actions to one person.
explanations.b: Disabling audit logs removes evidence of account access.
explanations.c: Federated sessions preserve identity context in audit logs when session names and assignments are configured properly. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Anonymous identity does not provide the needed workforce attribution.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A machine workload uses web identity federation from Kubernetes to call AWS APIs. Which access pattern is appropriate?

answers.text: Mount the node instance profile credentials into every pod intentionally
Store administrator access keys in a ConfigMap
Use a human IAM Identity Center permission set as the pod credential
IAM roles for service accounts or equivalent web identity role assumption

explanations.a: Sharing node credentials with all pods weakens workload isolation.
explanations.b: ConfigMaps are not secure long-term credential stores.
explanations.c: Workload federation should use machine identity patterns rather than human workforce assignments.
explanations.d: Web identity role assumption gives pods temporary AWS credentials tied to their service account identity. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A platform team lets application teams create IAM roles but must prevent them from granting permissions outside approved boundaries. What should be used?

answers.text: IAM permissions boundaries on roles created by delegated teams
A naming convention that includes least-privilege in every role name
A CloudWatch dashboard that lists created roles
An S3 lifecycle rule for IAM policy documents

explanations.a: Permissions boundaries define the maximum permissions an identity can receive, enabling safer delegation. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Names can signal intent but do not restrict permissions.
explanations.c: Visibility alone does not prevent excessive role permissions.
explanations.d: S3 lifecycle rules do not restrict IAM permissions.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A developer can attach policies to a role, but an applicable permissions boundary denies s3:DeleteBucket. What happens if the identity policy allows s3:DeleteBucket?

answers.text: The identity policy always overrides the boundary
The action remains denied because the boundary limits maximum effective permissions
The action succeeds if the console session is long enough
The action is allowed when the bucket is encrypted

explanations.a: An allow in an identity policy cannot exceed the maximum allowed by the boundary.
explanations.b: A permissions boundary constrains the permissions granted by identity policies. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Session duration does not bypass the permissions boundary.
explanations.d: Encryption status does not override IAM boundary evaluation.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An organization delegates creation of Lambda execution roles to development teams. What boundary should be included?

answers.text: A boundary that allows iam:* on all resources
No boundary because Lambda roles are machine identities
A boundary that allows only required service actions and prevents privilege escalation paths
A boundary attached only after production incidents

explanations.a: Broad IAM permissions can let teams escape delegation controls.
explanations.b: Machine roles can still be overprivileged and need guardrails.
explanations.c: Delegated role creation must restrict sensitive permissions such as IAM modification, broad PassRole, and unrelated administrative actions. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Delayed boundaries leave a window for excessive permissions.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A security team wants account owners to manage project IAM roles but not change the boundary policy. What policy design is needed?

answers.text: Let account owners delete the boundary before creating roles
Use only a verbal agreement about allowed permissions
Make the boundary policy public and editable by every principal
Allow role management while denying changes to the boundary and its attachment requirements

explanations.a: Deleting the boundary removes the delegated control.
explanations.b: Verbal guidance does not enforce delegation limits.
explanations.c: Broad edit rights let the boundary be weakened or removed.
explanations.d: Delegation should permit approved role operations while protecting the control that limits maximum permissions. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A CloudFormation template creates roles for application teams. How can the template enforce delegated permission limits?

answers.text: Attach the approved permissions boundary to created roles
Output the role name and ask teams to add the boundary later
Use a tag named BoundaryAttached without attaching a boundary
Store the boundary ARN in a README only

explanations.a: Including the boundary in IaC ensures roles created by the stack stay within the approved maximum permission set. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Manual follow-up can be missed and leaves roles unrestricted.
explanations.c: A tag does not enforce permission limits.
explanations.d: Documentation does not apply the boundary to the role.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An access review finds several delegated roles with boundaries but overly broad resource patterns within the boundary. What should be improved?

answers.text: Remove all boundaries because they were imperfect
Tighten the boundary and identity policies based on actual access requirements
Grant AdministratorAccess to simplify reviews
Hide the roles from IAM Access Analyzer

explanations.a: Imperfect boundaries should be refined rather than abandoned.
explanations.b: Boundaries limit maximum access, but both the boundary and attached policies need review to maintain least privilege. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: AdministratorAccess increases risk and defeats delegated control.
explanations.d: Hiding roles prevents visibility rather than improving permissions.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An organization must prevent all member accounts from disabling CloudTrail. Which control is appropriate?

answers.text: A CloudWatch dashboard showing trail status only
A local IAM policy attached to one audit role
An SCP that denies CloudTrail stop and delete actions with controlled exceptions
A tag on the CloudTrail trail named DoNotDisable

explanations.a: A dashboard provides visibility but does not block disabling actions.
explanations.b: A policy on one role does not constrain every principal in member accounts.
explanations.c: An SCP can set an organization-wide maximum permission that member account administrators cannot exceed. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Tags do not prevent control-plane API calls by themselves.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A production OU should allow EC2 only in approved Regions. What SCP design should be used?

answers.text: Allow every Region and rely on monthly manual review
Deny all AWS actions in every Region
Use subnet route tables to block AWS API calls in other Regions
Deny actions outside approved Regions while preserving required global service exceptions

explanations.a: Manual review detects issues after they happen and does not prevent unapproved usage.
explanations.b: A blanket deny would prevent production workloads from operating.
explanations.c: Route tables do not govern control-plane API authorization across Regions.
explanations.d: Region restriction SCPs can enforce approved locations but must account for global services and exception requirements. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A developer with AdministratorAccess in a member account cannot create an internet gateway because an SCP denies it. Why?

answers.text: SCPs limit the maximum permissions available to identities in the account
AdministratorAccess is stronger than every organization policy
The CLI is malfunctioning because SCPs are present
Internet gateways can be created only from the management account

explanations.a: AdministratorAccess in an identity policy cannot allow an action that an applicable SCP denies. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Organization policies constrain local administrators when they apply.
explanations.c: The CLI is working; authorization evaluation denies the action.
explanations.d: Member accounts can create internet gateways unless policies deny the action.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A security team wants to prevent creation of IAM users with console passwords in workload accounts. Which policy can enforce this broadly?

answers.text: A reminder in the account onboarding email
SCP denying IAM user and login profile creation in target OUs
A security group rule blocking port 443
A CloudWatch metric filter on application logs only

explanations.a: Email guidance does not enforce the restriction.
explanations.b: An SCP can prevent account-level principals from creating long-term human IAM users where federation is required. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Network rules do not govern IAM user creation APIs.
explanations.d: Application logs do not prevent IAM control-plane changes.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An SCP denies s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock changes. A central security role must still update the setting during onboarding. What should the SCP include?

answers.text: Remove the SCP for every account during onboarding and forget to reapply it
Allow every role to bypass the deny if it uses the console
A condition-based exception for the approved central security role
Use a bucket naming convention as the exception mechanism

explanations.a: Removing the control broadly creates a governance gap.
explanations.b: Console use does not make an action safe or authorized.
explanations.c: SCPs can include targeted exceptions so trusted automation can perform required baseline actions. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Names do not authenticate the automation principal.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An SCP rollout blocks a production deployment pipeline unexpectedly. What should the DevOps engineer do?

answers.text: Immediately delete every SCP in the organization
Ignore the deployment failure because SCPs are security-only
Grant root access to the pipeline to bypass the SCP
Review denied actions in CloudTrail and test SCP changes in lower-risk OUs before broad rollout

explanations.a: Removing all SCPs eliminates important governance controls.
explanations.b: SCPs directly affect operational automation and must be tested.
explanations.c: Root access does not bypass applicable SCP denies in member accounts.
explanations.d: SCP changes should be validated with evidence of affected actions before organization-wide enforcement. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An application role currently allows s3:* on all buckets but only needs to read one artifact bucket. What should be changed?

answers.text: Limit actions to required read operations and resources to the specific artifact bucket objects
Keep s3:* because the role belongs to an application
Add more wildcard services to avoid future changes
Move the permissions into the role name

explanations.a: Least privilege scopes both the actions and resources to what the workload actually needs. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Application roles still need least-privilege permissions.
explanations.c: Broadening access increases blast radius and violates least privilege.
explanations.d: Role names do not authorize or restrict AWS actions.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A CodeBuild project must push images to one ECR repository. Which policy design is best?

answers.text: AdministratorAccess for all build projects
Allow only the required ECR push actions on the target repository and required authorization call
A policy that allows ecr:* on every repository in every account
A policy that allows only CloudWatch dashboard edits

explanations.a: AdministratorAccess gives the build far more power than image publishing requires.
explanations.b: A build role should have the minimal ECR actions needed to authenticate and publish the image to the intended repository. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Repository-wide wildcard access increases damage if the build role is compromised.
explanations.d: Dashboard edits do not authorize ECR image publishing.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A DevOps role needs to pass only approved execution roles to Lambda. What IAM condition should be considered?

answers.text: Allow iam:PassRole on all roles with no service condition
Store allowed role names in build logs only
iam:PassedToService and resource scoping for approved roles
Use MFA presence as the only control for all role passing

explanations.a: Broad PassRole can enable privilege escalation through more powerful roles.
explanations.b: Logs do not enforce PassRole restrictions.
explanations.c: PassRole permissions should restrict which roles can be passed and to which AWS service. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: MFA can help human access, but PassRole still needs resource and service scoping.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A policy grants dynamodb:* because the application might need more actions later. What is the better approach?

answers.text: Keep broad permissions to avoid all future reviews
Deny all DynamoDB actions to every workload
Move data access decisions into a dashboard title
Grant the specific DynamoDB actions required and update through reviewed change control when needs change

explanations.a: Avoiding reviews trades convenience for excessive access.
explanations.b: A blanket deny would break the application rather than implement precise access.
explanations.c: Dashboard titles do not enforce data access permissions.
explanations.d: Least privilege should reflect current requirements and evolve through controlled updates. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A team needs to identify unused permissions in a production role. Which service can help analyze last-accessed activity?

answers.text: IAM Access Analyzer policy generation or service last accessed information
S3 Transfer Acceleration
Route 53 health checks
ECR tag immutability

explanations.a: Access analysis can reveal permissions that are not used and help refine policies. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Transfer Acceleration improves object transfers and does not analyze IAM permissions.
explanations.c: Health checks monitor endpoints and not IAM policy usage.
explanations.d: Tag immutability protects image references but does not identify unused permissions.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A Lambda function writes to one CloudWatch Logs log group and reads one secret. What is the best policy scope?

answers.text: secretsmanager:* on all secrets and logs:* on all log groups
logs permissions for the function log group and secretsmanager read permission for the specific secret
No execution role because Lambda is managed
A public resource policy on every secret

explanations.a: Broad secret and log permissions expose unrelated data and actions.
explanations.b: Specific resources and actions reduce exposure compared with broad account-wide access. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Lambda functions need an execution role for AWS API access.
explanations.d: Public secret access would expose sensitive data.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A company wants developers to access only resources tagged with their project name. Which pattern supports this?

answers.text: One shared administrator role for all developers
Manual review of every console click
ABAC using IAM policy conditions on resource and principal tags
Security group names matching project names

explanations.a: A shared administrator role removes project-level separation.
explanations.b: Manual review is not scalable authorization enforcement.
explanations.c: Attribute-based access control can compare principal and resource tags to authorize project-scoped access. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Security group names do not authorize AWS API access by project.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An operations team has roles named ReadOnly, PowerUser, and IncidentResponder. What access pattern is this?

answers.text: ABAC based only on matching tags
Network routing policy
Object lifecycle management
RBAC

explanations.a: ABAC uses attributes such as tags rather than named job roles as the primary decision point.
explanations.b: Routing policies direct traffic and do not define human permission roles.
explanations.c: Lifecycle rules manage data retention and not role-based access.
explanations.d: Role-based access control grants permissions according to job functions or operational roles. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A developer assumes a role with a project tag in the session. Policies allow access when the session project tag matches the resource tag. What must be controlled?

answers.text: Who can set session tags and which tag values are allowed
Allow every caller to set any project tag
Ignore resource tags during authorization
Use only free-form role descriptions for authorization

explanations.a: ABAC depends on trustworthy attributes, so session tagging permissions must be restricted and validated. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Unrestricted tag setting lets callers impersonate other projects.
explanations.c: Ignoring resource tags removes the project matching control.
explanations.d: Descriptions are metadata and do not enforce tag-based access.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A new employee changes from developer to incident responder. Which access model simplifies permission changes?

answers.text: Create a new long-term access key for every responsibility
Assign the user to a different federated group or permission set
Edit every resource policy manually for the person's name
Disable federation and share the response role password

explanations.a: More long-term keys increase credential management risk.
explanations.b: RBAC through groups or permission sets allows access to change with job function assignments. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Per-person resource edits do not scale and are error-prone.
explanations.d: Shared role passwords are not auditable and undermine identity controls.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A team combines RBAC for job function and ABAC for project scoping. Why is this useful?

answers.text: ABAC removes the need to control tag creation
RBAC automatically encrypts every resource
RBAC defines what actions a person can perform, while ABAC narrows where those actions apply
Using both patterns guarantees no policy review is needed

explanations.a: ABAC is only reliable when attributes are governed.
explanations.b: RBAC authorizes actions and does not perform encryption.
explanations.c: Combining role and attribute controls can enforce both job responsibility and project ownership. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Combined access models still require testing and periodic review.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A policy allows stopping EC2 instances only when aws:ResourceTag/Environment equals Development. What access model does this illustrate?

answers.text: Public key infrastructure
Static routing
Backup retention
ABAC

explanations.a: PKI manages certificates and keys, not tag-based EC2 authorization.
explanations.b: Routing controls network paths and not tag-based authorization.
explanations.c: Retention controls recovery point age and not authorization based on resource tags.
explanations.d: The decision uses a resource attribute to determine whether the action is allowed. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An application stores a database password in Secrets Manager. The security team requires periodic rotation without code changes. What should be configured?

answers.text: Secrets Manager rotation with a rotation Lambda or supported integration
Hardcode the new password into each deployment package
Email the rotated password to every developer
Store the password in an EC2 tag and change the tag monthly

explanations.a: Secrets Manager rotation can update the secret and target credential while applications continue retrieving the current secret value. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Hardcoding requires code changes and risks exposing the credential.
explanations.c: Email distribution exposes secrets and does not automate machine identity rotation.
explanations.d: Tags are visible metadata and are not secure secret storage.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A CI job uses an IAM access key for a machine user. The team wants to remove long-term keys. What is the better design?

answers.text: Make the access key never expire so rotation is unnecessary
Use an assumable role that provides temporary credentials to the CI job
Place the key in build logs so failures are easier to debug
Use the account root access key for every CI job

explanations.a: Nonrotating long-term keys increase compromise risk.
explanations.b: Temporary role credentials reduce long-term credential exposure and can be scoped to the job's actions. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Build logs should not contain secrets.
explanations.d: Root access keys are excessive and dangerous for automation.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A secret rotation succeeds in Secrets Manager but the application still uses old credentials until restart. What should be reviewed?

answers.text: Only the secret description length
Only the Route 53 record TTL
Application credential caching and refresh behavior
Only CloudFront cache invalidation

explanations.a: Description length does not control application refresh behavior.
explanations.b: DNS caching does not explain database credential caching inside the application.
explanations.c: Rotation only helps at runtime if applications retrieve or refresh the updated secret according to their credential lifecycle. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Invalidating content cache does not refresh database credentials.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A machine identity must access AWS APIs from an ECS task. Which credential delivery mechanism should be used?

answers.text: The container image label containing an access key
A developer's IAM user key mounted into the container
A public S3 object with the credentials
ECS task role

explanations.a: Image labels can expose long-term credentials to anyone who can pull or inspect the image.
explanations.b: Personal keys in containers weaken accountability and rotation.
explanations.c: Public objects must not contain credentials.
explanations.d: An ECS task role provides temporary credentials to the task without sharing host or static credentials. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A credential rotation workflow changes a database password but fails to test the new credential before marking success. What should be added?

answers.text: A validation step that authenticates with the new credential before finalizing rotation
A random sleep step with no validation
A log statement printing the new password
Deletion of the previous secret version before testing

explanations.a: Rotation workflows should verify that the new credential works so applications are not pointed to broken secrets. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Waiting does not prove the rotated credential is usable.
explanations.c: Printing the secret exposes it and still does not safely validate application access.
explanations.d: Deleting the old version before validation can remove rollback options.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A workload uses STS credentials from an assumed role. What operational practice is important?

answers.text: Disable CloudTrail because credentials are temporary
Set appropriate session duration and monitor unusual role assumption activity
Use unlimited session duration for every role
Share one session token across all workloads

explanations.a: Temporary credentials still generate important audit events.
explanations.b: Temporary credentials still need lifecycle tuning and audit monitoring for suspicious use. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Unlimited sessions would reduce the security benefit of temporary credentials.
explanations.d: Shared tokens weaken isolation and accountability.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A privileged human role can modify production security controls. What access control should be required?

answers.text: A permanent console password shared by the team
An unauthenticated public function URL that grants the role
MFA-protected federation or role assumption with monitored privileged access
A role trust policy that allows every AWS account

explanations.a: Shared passwords lack individual accountability and are weak for privileged access.
explanations.b: Public unauthenticated privilege elevation would be unsafe.
explanations.c: Privileged human access should use strong authentication and produce auditable temporary sessions. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Broad trust expands who can attempt privileged access.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An EC2 instance needs to access S3 without storing credentials on disk. What should be used?

answers.text: A plaintext access key stored in /etc/profile
A human federation token copied into user data
A bucket name that includes the word trusted
IAM instance profile

explanations.a: Plaintext keys on disk are exposed to local compromise and require manual rotation.
explanations.b: Human session tokens are not workload identity and can expire unpredictably.
explanations.c: Bucket names do not authenticate the instance.
explanations.d: An instance profile supplies temporary role credentials to EC2 through the metadata service. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A security team wants to prevent use of long-term access keys for human administrators. Which approach supports this?

answers.text: Use IAM Identity Center or federation with roles and require MFA
Create a new access key for every administrator each week
Let administrators share one key and rotate it yearly
Store administrator keys in public CI variables

explanations.a: Federated role access avoids long-term human keys and supports centralized MFA and auditability. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Frequent key creation still leaves long-term key handling and distribution problems.
explanations.c: Shared keys reduce accountability and remain long-term secrets.
explanations.d: Public CI variables would expose privileged credentials.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A role trust policy allows sts:AssumeRole from a partner account. What additional control reduces confused-deputy risk?

answers.text: Remove all conditions from the trust policy
Require an external ID condition
Use a public role name as the only secret
Allow root principals from every account

explanations.a: Fewer trust conditions increase the chance of unintended role assumption.
explanations.b: An external ID helps ensure the partner assumes the role only for the intended customer context. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Role names are not secret and do not prevent confused-deputy scenarios.
explanations.d: Broad trust increases exposure and bypasses the partner-specific control.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A developer assumes a production break-glass role. What should happen operationally?

answers.text: Suppress CloudTrail events for break-glass use
Make the role session last indefinitely
Generate audit events and notifications for privileged role assumption
Reuse the same session for every engineer

explanations.a: Privileged access needs more auditability, not less.
explanations.b: Shorter controlled sessions reduce exposure for emergency access.
explanations.c: Break-glass access should be visible so teams can review why and how it was used. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Shared sessions remove individual accountability.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An application running on EKS should use AWS permissions specific to one Kubernetes service account. What mechanism fits?

answers.text: The node instance profile shared by every pod
A ConfigMap containing AWS access keys
A human MFA token mounted into the pod
IAM roles for service accounts

explanations.a: Node-wide credentials can overgrant permissions to unrelated pods.
explanations.b: ConfigMaps are not a secure store for static AWS credentials.
explanations.c: Human MFA tokens are not appropriate machine identity credentials.
explanations.d: IAM roles for service accounts map Kubernetes service accounts to scoped IAM roles for pod-level AWS access. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A web application must block common malicious HTTP requests before they reach an ALB. Which service should be used?

answers.text: AWS WAF associated with the web entry point
A security group rule that parses SQL injection payloads
An IAM permission boundary on the ALB
S3 Object Lock on access logs

explanations.a: AWS WAF can inspect web requests and apply managed or custom rules before traffic reaches the application. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Security groups filter network ports and addresses, not HTTP payload patterns.
explanations.c: Permissions boundaries govern IAM permissions and do not inspect web requests.
explanations.d: Object Lock protects log retention and does not block live HTTP attacks.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A VPC requires centralized inspection for outbound and east-west traffic using managed network firewall rules. Which service fits?

answers.text: AWS CodeArtifact
AWS Network Firewall
Amazon Macie
AWS Backup Vault Lock

explanations.a: CodeArtifact stores software packages and does not inspect VPC traffic.
explanations.b: AWS Network Firewall provides managed network traffic filtering and inspection for VPC traffic paths. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Macie discovers sensitive data in S3 and does not filter network flows.
explanations.d: Vault Lock protects backups and does not inspect network packets.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A private subnet should not receive unsolicited inbound internet traffic, but instances need outbound internet updates. Which network pattern fits?

answers.text: Assign public IPs to every instance and open all inbound ports
Use a bucket policy as the only network boundary
Route through a NAT gateway with restrictive security groups
Disable all route tables

explanations.a: Public IPs and open ports expose instances directly to the internet.
explanations.b: Bucket policies do not control EC2 subnet inbound traffic.
explanations.c: A NAT gateway supports outbound access from private subnets while security groups restrict inbound exposure. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Instances need valid routes for required network communication.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An EC2 security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 inbound SSH in production. What should be changed?

answers.text: Open RDP to the internet as well for consistency
Rename the security group to private
Move the same rule into a network ACL without review
Restrict administrative access to approved networks or use Session Manager without inbound SSH

explanations.a: Adding more open administrative ports increases exposure.
explanations.b: Names do not change network reachability.
explanations.c: A broad allow in another control plane does not solve administrative exposure.
explanations.d: Administrative access should be limited or moved to a managed access path that avoids broad internet exposure. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A public API needs DDoS protection and application-layer filtering. Which combination is appropriate?

answers.text: AWS Shield for DDoS protection and AWS WAF for HTTP filtering
Secrets Manager and Parameter Store only
CloudTrail log file validation only
EBS encryption and lifecycle policies only

explanations.a: Shield addresses DDoS protection, while WAF provides web request inspection and rule enforcement. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Secret stores do not absorb DDoS attacks or filter HTTP requests.
explanations.c: Log validation protects audit integrity and does not filter live traffic.
explanations.d: Storage encryption and lifecycle do not protect web entry points from DDoS and HTTP attacks.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A network ACL blocks ephemeral response ports from a private subnet. What operational symptom can this cause?

answers.text: IAM role assumptions automatically become public
Allowed requests can fail because return traffic is blocked
KMS keys rotate every minute
CloudTrail stops recording all management events

explanations.a: NACL response port blocking does not change IAM trust policies.
explanations.b: Network ACLs are stateless, so both request and response paths must be allowed. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Network ACLs do not control key rotation schedules.
explanations.d: Traffic filtering does not disable CloudTrail management event logging.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A public ALB requires an automatically renewed TLS certificate for a company domain. Which service should manage the certificate?

answers.text: AWS Backup
Amazon SQS
AWS Certificate Manager
AWS CodeArtifact

explanations.a: Backup manages recovery points and does not issue public TLS certificates.
explanations.b: SQS stores messages and does not manage certificates.
explanations.c: ACM can provision and renew public TLS certificates for supported integrated services such as ALB. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: CodeArtifact stores packages and does not terminate TLS for ALB.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A certificate imported into ACM is nearing expiration. What should the DevOps engineer remember?

answers.text: Imported certificates always renew automatically without external action
Certificate expiration affects only billing reports
CloudWatch alarms cannot monitor certificate expiration
Imported certificates are not automatically renewed by ACM

explanations.a: Imported certificates require renewal outside ACM.
explanations.b: Expired certificates can break TLS connections for clients.
explanations.c: Certificate expiration can be monitored through available metrics or events depending on the service integration.
explanations.d: ACM can renew eligible ACM-issued public certificates, but imported certificates require external renewal and reimport. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A private microservice mesh needs internally trusted certificates. Which option can issue private certificates under AWS-managed PKI?

answers.text: AWS Private Certificate Authority with ACM integration
S3 Versioning
ECR scan-on-push
Route 53 weighted routing only

explanations.a: AWS Private CA can issue private certificates for internal trust models and integrate with ACM workflows. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Versioning protects object history and does not issue certificates.
explanations.c: Image scanning detects vulnerabilities and does not create private PKI.
explanations.d: Weighted routing distributes DNS responses and does not issue certificates.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A DevOps team needs to rotate TLS certificates with no application downtime. What deployment practice helps?

answers.text: Delete the old certificate first and wait for errors
Attach the new certificate to the load balancer before removing the old certificate
Store the private key in application logs for backup
Disable HTTPS during rotation

explanations.a: Removing the active certificate before replacement can interrupt TLS.
explanations.b: Overlapping certificate deployment keeps TLS available while clients transition to the new certificate. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Private keys must not be logged.
explanations.d: Turning off HTTPS violates encryption-in-transit expectations.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A certificate validation DNS record is deleted from Route 53. What is the likely risk for an ACM-issued public certificate?

answers.text: The certificate immediately becomes a KMS key
CloudTrail management events stop
Future managed renewal can fail
All S3 buckets become public

explanations.a: DNS validation records do not convert certificates into KMS keys.
explanations.b: Deleting a validation record does not disable CloudTrail.
explanations.c: ACM needs domain validation to remain in place for managed renewal of public certificates. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Certificate DNS validation does not change bucket policies.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A regulated workload requires control of cryptographic keys in dedicated hardware outside the shared KMS service boundary. Which service should be evaluated?

answers.text: AWS WAF
Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon Macie
AWS CloudHSM

explanations.a: WAF filters web requests and does not provide dedicated HSM key management.
explanations.b: GuardDuty detects threats and does not host cryptographic keys.
explanations.c: Macie discovers sensitive S3 data and does not provide dedicated key hardware.
explanations.d: CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules for workloads that require direct HSM control. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A data lake contains unknown customer data in S3. The team needs to find buckets that might contain PII. Which service should be used?

answers.text: Amazon Macie
AWS Shield
Amazon RDS Proxy
AWS CodeDeploy

explanations.a: Macie can discover and classify sensitive data such as PII in S3 at scale. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Shield protects against DDoS and does not classify S3 object contents.
explanations.c: RDS Proxy manages database connections and does not scan S3 data for PII.
explanations.d: CodeDeploy deploys applications and does not discover sensitive data.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A database backup is encrypted with a customer managed KMS key. What must be true for a restore role?

answers.text: The restore role must know the key alias text only
The restore role must have permissions to use the KMS key for decryption
The restore role needs public internet access to decrypt locally
The restore role needs permission to change DNS TTL

explanations.a: Knowing an alias does not grant cryptographic permissions.
explanations.b: Encrypted data cannot be restored unless the restoring principal can use the protecting key. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: KMS authorization is not replaced by public internet access.
explanations.d: DNS TTL does not decrypt backups.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A team wants different data retention and encryption rules based on data sensitivity. What should come first?

answers.text: Apply the same retention and access controls to every dataset without analysis
Remove labels from all data to simplify storage
Data classification that identifies sensitivity and required controls
Store classification decisions only in personal notes

explanations.a: Uniform controls can overretain low-risk data or underprotect sensitive data.
explanations.b: Removing labels makes it harder to apply appropriate protections.
explanations.c: Classification guides which encryption, access, retention, and monitoring controls should apply to each dataset. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Personal notes do not provide scalable policy enforcement.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An S3 bucket stores sensitive reports. Which access-control combination is appropriate?

answers.text: Public read access with encryption enabled
No audit logging because reports are encrypted
A bucket name that includes confidential with no policy controls
Block Public Access, least-privilege bucket policies, encryption, and audit logging

explanations.a: Encryption at rest does not make public read access safe.
explanations.b: Encryption does not replace access auditing.
explanations.c: Names do not enforce confidentiality.
explanations.d: Sensitive data needs layered controls that prevent public exposure, restrict access, protect data at rest, and record activity. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A KMS key policy allows every principal in the account to administer the key. What is the concern?

answers.text: Overbroad key administration can allow unauthorized policy changes or key deletion
The key will stop encrypting because too many principals can administer it
S3 cannot use customer managed KMS keys
CloudWatch metrics cannot show KMS usage

explanations.a: Key administrators can affect access and availability of encrypted data, so key administration must be tightly scoped. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: The operational issue is control-plane risk, not automatic encryption failure.
explanations.c: S3 can use customer managed KMS keys when configured properly.
explanations.d: KMS usage can be audited and monitored through AWS logging and metrics sources.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A data protection policy requires separation between data readers and key administrators. What design supports this?

answers.text: One shared administrator role for every data and key operation
Distinct IAM roles and KMS key policies for data access and key administration
Hardcoded KMS grants in application source with no review
Disable encryption so key administration is unnecessary

explanations.a: Shared broad administration defeats separation of duties.
explanations.b: Separation of duties reduces the chance that one principal can both access data and weaken key controls. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Unreviewed hardcoding weakens key access governance.
explanations.d: Removing encryption violates the data protection objective.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A security baseline must enable GuardDuty in every current and future account. What automation should be used?

answers.text: Ask each account owner to enable GuardDuty manually whenever they remember
Enable GuardDuty only in the management account
Organization-wide GuardDuty administration with automated enablement for member accounts
Store GuardDuty setup steps in a private note

explanations.a: Manual enablement leaves gaps and is difficult to verify at scale.
explanations.b: One account's enablement does not protect every member account.
explanations.c: Delegated or organization-wide administration enables consistent GuardDuty coverage across accounts. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Private notes do not apply controls across accounts.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A company wants baseline AWS Config rules deployed to every account and Region. Which deployment pattern fits?

answers.text: Individual console clicks in each account
A single local script that stores results only on a laptop
A public wiki page with rule names
CloudFormation StackSets or organization-based Config rule deployment

explanations.a: Manual setup is slow and can drift across accounts.
explanations.b: Laptop-only automation lacks centralized state and repeatability.
explanations.c: Documentation does not deploy Config rules.
explanations.d: Centralized IaC deployment can apply compliance rules consistently across the organization. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A multi-account environment needs Security Hub standards enabled and findings centralized. What should be configured?

answers.text: Security Hub delegated administrator and organization integration
A separate unmanaged Security Hub configuration in only one workload account
CloudFront signed cookies
EBS default encryption only

explanations.a: Security Hub organization integration centralizes standards and findings across member accounts. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: One account's configuration does not aggregate organization-wide findings.
explanations.c: Signed cookies control content access and not security finding aggregation.
explanations.d: EBS encryption is a data protection control but not Security Hub centralization.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A baseline requires all accounts to have S3 Block Public Access enabled. How should drift be remediated?

answers.text: Rely on developers to notice public buckets during feature work
Detect drift with Config or Security Hub and remediate with approved automation
Make public buckets acceptable if they are tagged
Disable Config to reduce findings

explanations.a: Developer observation is not a scalable drift control.
explanations.b: Automated detection and remediation keep account-level controls aligned at scale. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Tags do not make unintended public access safe.
explanations.d: Disabling detection hides drift rather than fixing it.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A security automation role in a delegated admin account remediates member account findings. What must be configured?

answers.text: Root credentials from every member account stored in the admin account
Public resource policies on every target resource
Cross-account trust and least-privilege permissions in target accounts
One broad unrestricted role trusted by every principal

explanations.a: Root credential storage is unsafe and unnecessary.
explanations.b: Public access is not a safe remediation authorization model.
explanations.c: The automation needs authorized access to target accounts, scoped to the remediation actions. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Broad trust expands who can trigger sensitive remediation.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A platform team wants new accounts to automatically receive security baselines during onboarding. Which approach fits?

answers.text: Wait until the first audit to configure security baselines
Ask teams to copy controls from screenshots
Only tag the account SecurityReady without deploying controls
Control Tower account customization or account vending pipeline with StackSets

explanations.a: Delayed baselines leave new accounts exposed.
explanations.b: Screenshot-based configuration is not reliable automation.
explanations.c: Tags alone do not implement security services or policies.
explanations.d: Account onboarding automation can apply security services, logging, and guardrails immediately when accounts are created. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A public web application needs protection from SQL injection, known bad IPs, and volumetric attacks. Which layered design is appropriate?

answers.text: AWS WAF managed rules with AWS Shield and network controls at the edge and VPC
Only an IAM password policy
Only EBS encryption on web server volumes
Only a dashboard that shows request counts

explanations.a: Defense in depth combines web-layer filtering, DDoS protection, and network restrictions so no single control carries all protection. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Password policy does not inspect web traffic or absorb DDoS attacks.
explanations.c: Storage encryption does not filter malicious HTTP requests.
explanations.d: Visibility alone does not block or mitigate attacks.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A sensitive API is fronted by API Gateway and Lambda. What defense-in-depth controls should be combined?

answers.text: Only Lambda reserved concurrency
Authentication and authorization, WAF where appropriate, least-privilege Lambda role, encryption, and logging
Only public invocation with no logging
Only changing the API stage name

explanations.a: Concurrency limits can protect capacity but do not provide authentication, authorization, or data protection.
explanations.b: Layered controls protect the entry point, execution identity, data, and audit trail. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Unauthenticated public access and missing logs weaken security posture.
explanations.d: Stage names do not enforce security controls.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A VPC workload processes sensitive data and must limit egress to approved domains or services. What controls can be combined?

answers.text: One unrestricted NAT gateway route with no monitoring
A Secrets Manager secret named ApprovedDomains
Security groups, route controls, VPC endpoints, and AWS Network Firewall where required
Only an S3 lifecycle policy

explanations.a: Unrestricted egress can allow unintended destinations.
explanations.b: A secret name does not enforce network routing or filtering.
explanations.c: Network egress control often needs multiple layers to restrict paths and inspect or route traffic appropriately. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Lifecycle policies manage object age and do not restrict network egress.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A team wants to detect and investigate suspicious account activity. Which services can be combined?

answers.text: CodeArtifact, ECR lifecycle rules, and Route 53 TTL only
Only ALB target group stickiness
Only EC2 user data comments
GuardDuty, CloudTrail, Detective, and Security Hub

explanations.a: Package storage, image cleanup, and DNS TTL do not provide broad threat investigation.
explanations.b: Stickiness affects traffic routing and not security investigation.
explanations.c: Comments do not detect or investigate security activity.
explanations.d: Threat detection, audit logs, investigation graphs, and finding aggregation provide complementary security visibility. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A control requires that S3 buckets cannot be public and findings must be investigated. What layered approach fits?

answers.text: S3 Block Public Access, bucket policies, Config rules, Security Hub findings, and audit logs
Only a bucket naming convention
Only object compression
Only application unit tests

explanations.a: Preventive settings, resource policies, compliance evaluation, centralized findings, and logs work together to prevent and detect exposure. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Names do not prevent public access or create findings.
explanations.c: Compression does not control access or detect public exposure.
explanations.d: Unit tests do not continuously evaluate bucket access posture.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A defense-in-depth design for secrets should include which controls?

answers.text: Plaintext secrets in source control with branch protection only
Secrets Manager storage, KMS encryption, IAM-scoped access, rotation, and audit monitoring
Secrets in environment variable names and no rotation
One shared secret for every application forever

explanations.a: Branch protection does not make plaintext secrets safe.
explanations.b: Secret protection requires secure storage, cryptographic protection, restricted retrieval, lifecycle rotation, and usage visibility. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Environment variable names are visible metadata and do not provide secret rotation.
explanations.d: Shared nonrotating secrets increase blast radius and complicate incident response.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A company must find S3 buckets that contain sensitive personal data across many accounts. Which service should be automated?

answers.text: AWS WAF
AWS CodeDeploy
Amazon Macie
Amazon SQS

explanations.a: WAF filters web requests and does not classify stored S3 objects.
explanations.b: CodeDeploy manages deployments and does not discover sensitive data.
explanations.c: Macie can discover and classify sensitive data in S3 across accounts when configured for the organization. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: SQS queues messages and does not scan S3 buckets for sensitive data.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A Macie finding identifies credentials in an S3 object. What should the response workflow do?

answers.text: Publish the object publicly so more people can inspect it
Ignore the finding because the object is encrypted at rest
Delete the finding without triage
Notify security, restrict access if needed, and start credential rotation or containment

explanations.a: Public exposure increases the risk from discovered credentials.
explanations.b: Encryption at rest does not prevent authorized or accidental exposure of sensitive content.
explanations.c: Removing the finding does not address the sensitive data risk.
explanations.d: Sensitive credential discovery should drive containment and rotation so exposed secrets are no longer usable. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A data discovery job scans all buckets and creates excessive findings for test data. What should be improved?

answers.text: Classification scope, allow lists, and environment-aware severity handling
Disable sensitive data discovery everywhere
Treat every test finding as a production breach
Store all findings in a public bucket

explanations.a: Tuning discovery scope and classification logic keeps sensitive data detection actionable without hiding important findings. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Turning off discovery removes visibility into real sensitive data exposure.
explanations.c: Misclassified severity creates alert fatigue and poor prioritization.
explanations.d: Findings can contain sensitive context and should be protected.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A security team wants sensitive data findings routed to data owners. What must be present?

answers.text: Random bucket names with no owner tags
Consistent resource ownership metadata such as account, tags, or bucket mapping
Only the object's file extension
A single shared mailbox with no triage rules

explanations.a: Missing ownership metadata delays response.
explanations.b: Ownership metadata lets automation route findings to the team that can remediate the data exposure. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Extensions rarely identify the accountable owner.
explanations.d: A shared mailbox can become a backlog without ownership routing.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: Macie is enabled in one account, but the organization needs delegated administration. What should be configured?

answers.text: Separate unmanaged Macie setup only in a sandbox account
A Lambda layer named Macie
Macie administrator account and member account association through AWS Organizations
A Route 53 hosted zone for all bucket names

explanations.a: Sandbox-only configuration does not discover data across production accounts.
explanations.b: Layer naming does not enable sensitive data discovery.
explanations.c: Delegated administration centralizes sensitive data discovery management across accounts. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: DNS hosted zones do not centralize Macie administration.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A sensitive data discovery automation should avoid scanning data that violates residency rules by copying it to another Region. What design should be used?

answers.text: Copy every object to a central public Region before scanning
Download all data to a responder laptop for scanning
Disable encryption during scanning
Run discovery in place within approved Regions and protect findings with regional controls

explanations.a: Unnecessary cross-Region copying can violate residency and expose data.
explanations.b: Laptop downloads create uncontrolled copies of sensitive data.
explanations.c: Discovery should not require removing data protection controls.
explanations.d: Sensitive data discovery must respect data residency and keep findings protected without unnecessary data movement. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An S3 bucket must enforce encryption at rest with a customer managed KMS key. What should be configured?

answers.text: Default bucket encryption with SSE-KMS and a bucket policy that denies unencrypted uploads where required
A bucket name that includes encrypted
Public read access with TLS only
A lifecycle rule that immediately expires unencrypted objects

explanations.a: Default encryption and policy enforcement help ensure new objects are protected with the intended key. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Naming does not enforce encryption.
explanations.c: TLS protects transit but does not enforce encryption at rest.
explanations.d: Expiration after upload still permits noncompliant writes and can delete data unexpectedly.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A service-to-service API must encrypt traffic in transit. What should be used?

answers.text: EBS encryption only
TLS certificates and HTTPS or mutual TLS where required
A longer IAM role session name
S3 lifecycle transitions

explanations.a: EBS encryption protects block storage at rest and does not secure API traffic in transit.
explanations.b: TLS protects data in transit, and mutual TLS can authenticate both sides when the workload requires it. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Session name length does not encrypt network traffic.
explanations.d: Lifecycle transitions manage object storage class and not API transport encryption.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A database stores regulated data. Which encryption design is appropriate?

answers.text: Store the KMS key ID in a public dashboard
Disable encryption to improve troubleshooting
Enable database encryption with KMS and restrict key access to required roles
Use a security group name as the encryption key

explanations.a: Key identifiers are not sufficient protection and public exposure of operational details is unnecessary.
explanations.b: Troubleshooting should not require removing required data protection.
explanations.c: KMS-backed database encryption protects data at rest while key policies control who can administer or use the key. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Security group names do not provide cryptographic protection.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A pipeline provisions new EBS volumes across many accounts. How can encryption be enforced automatically?

answers.text: Ask every developer to remember to check a box
Only encrypt volumes after incidents
Use AMI names as proof of every volume's encryption state
Enable EBS encryption by default and validate with Config or preventive policies

explanations.a: Manual selection is inconsistent at scale.
explanations.b: Delayed encryption leaves data exposed before remediation.
explanations.c: AMI naming does not verify live EBS volume encryption.
explanations.d: Account or Region defaults plus compliance evaluation help ensure new volumes meet encryption requirements. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A KMS key is shared across accounts for encrypted artifact access. What policy configuration is needed?

answers.text: Key policy and IAM permissions that allow only approved cross-account roles to decrypt
Public key policy access for every AWS principal
Only S3 bucket versioning
Only a shared tag on the key and role

explanations.a: Cross-account KMS use requires both key trust and caller permissions scoped to approved roles. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Public decrypt access would expose encrypted artifacts.
explanations.c: Versioning does not grant KMS decrypt permission.
explanations.d: Tags can support conditions, but policy authorization still needs to be configured.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A DevOps team needs to rotate customer managed KMS keys without breaking encrypted data access. What should they understand?

answers.text: Rotation deletes all data encrypted with the previous material
KMS automatic key rotation preserves the key ID and keeps previous key material for decrypting existing data
Rotation requires every S3 object to be manually downloaded immediately
Rotation grants decrypt access to every administrator automatically

explanations.a: KMS retains old key material needed for decryption.
explanations.b: Managed rotation changes backing key material while maintaining decrypt capability for data encrypted under earlier material. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Automatic KMS rotation does not require immediate object download.
explanations.d: Rotation does not broaden authorization policies.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A compliance team needs an audit trail of who changed security group rules. Which service provides this control-plane history?

answers.text: Amazon Macie
AWS WAF logs only
AWS CloudTrail
EBS volume metrics

explanations.a: Macie discovers sensitive data in S3 and does not record all security group API changes.
explanations.b: WAF logs show web request evaluations and not EC2 security group management calls.
explanations.c: CloudTrail records management API calls such as security group rule changes and the principal that made them. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Volume metrics do not show who changed network rules.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A company needs continuous evaluation of whether resources comply with encryption and public-access rules. Which service is appropriate?

answers.text: AWS CodeArtifact
Amazon SQS long polling
AWS App Runner
AWS Config

explanations.a: CodeArtifact stores software packages and does not evaluate resource configuration compliance.
explanations.b: Long polling improves queue receive efficiency and not compliance evaluation.
explanations.c: App Runner hosts applications and does not provide broad configuration compliance evaluation.
explanations.d: AWS Config evaluates resource configuration against managed or custom rules and records configuration history. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An auditor asks whether CloudFormation-managed resources have been changed outside the template. Which feature helps identify this?

answers.text: CloudFormation drift detection
ECR image tag immutability
CloudFront geographic restrictions
AWS Backup copy jobs

explanations.a: Drift detection compares supported live resource properties with expected stack configuration. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Image tag immutability prevents tag overwrite and does not compare stack resources.
explanations.c: Geographic restrictions affect viewer access and not IaC drift.
explanations.d: Backup copies do not identify template drift.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A security team needs network connection metadata for an investigation. Which log source should be enabled?

answers.text: CloudFormation Outputs
VPC Flow Logs
Secrets Manager rotation history only
S3 Storage Lens only

explanations.a: Outputs expose stack values and do not record network flows.
explanations.b: VPC Flow Logs capture network flow metadata for supported network interfaces, subnets, or VPCs. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Rotation history does not capture network connections.
explanations.d: Storage Lens provides storage analytics and not VPC flow metadata.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A workload requires object-level audit of S3 reads and writes for a sensitive bucket. What CloudTrail feature is needed?

answers.text: Only CloudTrail management events
Only bucket default encryption
S3 data events for the bucket
Only VPC Flow Logs

explanations.a: Management events do not include all object-level S3 access activity.
explanations.b: Encryption protects objects but does not record every read and write.
explanations.c: CloudTrail data events capture object-level activity when enabled for selected resources. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Flow logs do not identify S3 object API operations.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A security audit needs centralized evidence across accounts. What architecture supports this?

answers.text: Independent local logs with no aggregation
A shared spreadsheet updated manually once per year
A single application dashboard for one account
Organization CloudTrail, centralized log archive, AWS Config aggregation, and Security Hub aggregation

explanations.a: Local-only evidence is harder to search and can be modified by account administrators.
explanations.b: Annual manual evidence is incomplete and stale.
explanations.c: One workload dashboard does not provide organization-wide audit evidence.
explanations.d: Centralized audit services collect management events, configuration state, and findings across the organization. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A security team wants to detect suspicious API activity, credential misuse, and anomalous behavior in AWS accounts. Which service is appropriate?

answers.text: Amazon GuardDuty
AWS CodeBuild
Amazon EFS
AWS Backup

explanations.a: GuardDuty analyzes events and network signals to identify potential threats such as credential misuse and anomalous activity. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: CodeBuild runs builds and does not provide managed threat detection.
explanations.c: EFS provides file storage and not account threat detection.
explanations.d: Backup protects recovery points and does not analyze suspicious API activity.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A container image in ECR should be checked for known vulnerabilities before deployment. Which service can help?

answers.text: Amazon Macie
Amazon Inspector enhanced scanning
AWS Shield
Route 53 Resolver

explanations.a: Macie focuses on sensitive data discovery in S3 rather than container image vulnerabilities.
explanations.b: Inspector can scan container images and report package vulnerabilities for supported configurations. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Shield protects against DDoS attacks and does not scan images.
explanations.d: Resolver handles DNS queries and does not assess container packages.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A team wants to identify S3 buckets shared with external principals. Which service helps analyze unintended access?

answers.text: Amazon RDS Performance Insights
EC2 Auto Scaling
IAM Access Analyzer
AWS DataSync

explanations.a: Performance Insights analyzes database performance and not external resource access.
explanations.b: Auto Scaling manages compute capacity and does not analyze resource policies.
explanations.c: Access Analyzer evaluates resource policies to identify access granted outside the intended zone of trust. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: DataSync moves data and does not review bucket policy exposure.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A Security Hub finding reports an unencrypted EBS volume. What should the response workflow do?

answers.text: Delete the finding without changing the volume or recording an exception
Make the volume public so auditors can review it
Ignore all medium findings forever
Route the finding to the owner and trigger approved remediation or exception handling

explanations.a: Removing the finding does not address the unencrypted data risk.
explanations.b: Public exposure increases risk and does not remediate encryption.
explanations.c: Persistent findings can represent real risk and require triage.
explanations.d: Security findings need ownership, remediation, or documented exception paths so risk is reduced or accepted formally. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: A company wants to investigate relationships among GuardDuty findings, CloudTrail activity, and affected resources. Which service supports investigation graphs?

answers.text: Amazon Detective
AWS CodeDeploy
Amazon CloudFront Functions
AWS Backup Audit Manager only

explanations.a: Detective helps analyze and visualize relationships among security findings, entities, and activity. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: CodeDeploy manages deployments and does not build security investigation graphs.
explanations.c: CloudFront Functions run edge code and do not investigate GuardDuty findings.
explanations.d: Backup audit reporting does not correlate GuardDuty entities and API activity.

questions.name: Security and Compliance
questions.text: An alert indicates an exposed access key was found in a public repository. Which immediate actions are appropriate?

answers.text: Leave the key active until the next scheduled rotation
Disable or rotate the key, investigate CloudTrail activity, and remove the exposed secret from the repository
Only rename the IAM user
Post the key in a ticket so more responders can test it

explanations.a: Waiting gives an attacker more time to use the exposed credential.
explanations.b: Exposed credentials require containment, audit of possible use, and removal from source history or public visibility. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Renaming does not invalidate the exposed access key.
explanations.d: Sharing the exposed key further increases risk.
